UPSTREAM: Staging: Gasket: shift wrapping bug in gasket_read_modify_write_64() This function only has one caller so mask_width is 1 and mask_shift is 32. Shifting an int by 32 bits is undefined, but I guess on GCC it wraps to 0x1? Anyway it's supposed to be 0x100000000. UPSTREAM: staging: gasket: add SPDX identifiers to all files. It's good to have SPDX identifiers in all files to make it easier to audit the kernel tree for correct licenses. Fix up the all of the staging gasket files to have a proper SPDX identifier, based on the license text in the file itself. The SPDX identifier is a legally binding shorthand, which can be used instead of the full boiler plate text. BUG=b:79253135 TEST=none CQ-DEPEND=CL:1153441 Cc: Rob Springer <rspringer@google.com> Cc: John Joseph <jnjoseph@google.com> Cc: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org> (cherry picked from commit 2dec0644e0c8083e0a9d3bbdd11aad2d850859e9) Signed-off-by: Zhongze Hu <frankhu@google.com> Change-Id: I400fb87d94afa15ae0cb88302287e7e913498de4 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1153443 Commit-Ready: Zhongze Hu <frankhu@google.com> Tested-by: Zhongze Hu <frankhu@google.com> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: staging: gasket: remove redundant license information Now that the SPDX tag is in all gasket files, that identifies the license in a specific and legally-defined manner. So the extra GPL text wording can be removed as it is no longer needed at all. This is done on a quest to remove the 700+ different ways that files in the kernel describe the GPL license text. And there's unneeded stuff like the address (sometimes incorrect) for the FSF which is never needed. BUG=b:79253135 TEST=none CQ-DEPEND=CL:1153443 Cc: Rob Springer <rspringer@google.com> Cc: John Joseph <jnjoseph@google.com> Cc: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org> (cherry picked from commit bf9c7a8673831acd67ad4a92b6acd85ffcde174c) Signed-off-by: Zhongze Hu <frankhu@google.com> Change-Id: Idf06573e3096e82c7bd47bc8c32d2eb4a1e63b9e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1153470 Commit-Ready: Zhongze Hu <frankhu@google.com> Tested-by: Zhongze Hu <frankhu@google.com> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org>

cros-kernel2: Add a use flag for debug objects The kernel has a debugging facility called debugobjects that's useful to detect improper usage of kernel objects such as timers, workqueues, RCU callbacks, etc. But the overhead isn't minimal because each object is tracked for it's entire lifetime, and sometimes even after it's freed, so put this behind a new useflag. autotest: Stage control file inside SSP container for skylab In skylab, control file name is passed in and autoserv finds the control file to execute using the name. When running a test with SSP, autoserv re-executes inside the container with somewhat modified commandline. For skylab, autoserv now passes in --control-file unchanged into the container. autoserv execution inside the container finds and stages the control file. Because the autotest checkout inside the container is from the test artifacts for the target build, this results in the control file being staged from the right build. BUG=chromium:871439 TEST=Manual.
